So worship Him. This is a straight path (19:36), that is, an upright religion in which there is no crookedness.

His words, Exalted: Then the factions differed among themselves (19:37). "Among" (min) is redundant, that is, "the factions differed between themselves". Qatādah said: that is, "what was between them"; so the sects of the People of the Book differed over the matter of Jesus (peace be upon him). The Jews with slander and the charge of sorcery; as for the Christians, the Nestorians among them said he is the son of God, the Melkites (al-Malkāniyyah) said he is the third of three, and the Jacobites said he is God. So the Christians went to excess and exaggerated, and the Jews fell short and belittled. This has already been treated in al-Nisāʾ.{{fn:At Qurʾān 4:157 and 4:171.}} Ibn ʿAbbās said: what is meant by "the factions" are those idolaters who banded together against the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and called him a liar.

So woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a tremendous day (19:37), that is, from witnessing the Day of Resurrection. "Witnessing" (mashhad) is here in the sense of the verbal noun, and shuhūd means presence. It is also possible that the presence is theirs, and that it is annexed to the adverb of time because it occurs within it, as one says "woe to so-and-so from the fighting of such-and-such a day", that is, from his presence on that day. It has been said that mashhad means the place which all creatures will witness, like maḥshar for the place to which creation is gathered. And it has been said: so woe to those who disbelieve from their presence at the great assembly in which they gathered for consultation and agreed upon disbelief in God and upon their saying that God is the third of three.

His words, Exalted: How clearly they will hear and see on the day they come to Us (19:38). Abū l-ʿAbbās{{fn:Abū l-ʿAbbās Thaʿlab, the Kufan grammarian.}} said: the Arabs use this form in the position of wonder, so they say "asmiʿ bi-Zayd" and "abṣir bi-Zayd", that is, "how well he hears and sees!" He said: so its meaning is that He caused His Prophet to wonder at them. Al-Kalbī said: on the Day of Resurrection there will be no one who hears better or sees better than they, when God, Blessed and Exalted, says to Jesus: Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God"? (5:116). It has been said that "hear" is in the sense of obedience, that is, "how obedient they will be to God on that day!" But the wrongdoers today (19:38) means in this world,

are in manifest error (19:38). And what error is more manifest than that a man should believe, of a person like himself, whom wombs carried, who ate and drank, who relieved himself and stood in need, that he is a god? Whoever is of this description is deaf and blind, but he will see and hear in the Hereafter when he beholds the punishment, though that will not avail him. Qatādah and others said this in meaning.

His words, Exalted: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided (19:39). It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: there is no one who enters the Fire but that he has a house in the Garden, and he regrets it. It has been said that the regret falls when a man is given his book in his left hand. when the matter will be decided, that is, when the reckoning has been concluded, and the people of the Garden have been admitted to the Garden and the people of the Fire to the Fire. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, from the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may God be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the people of the Garden have entered the Garden and the people of the Fire the Fire, death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection as though it were a ram of mingled black and white, and it will be made to stand between the Garden and the Fire, and it will be said: O people of the Garden, do you recognise this? They will crane their necks and look and say: Yes, this is death. He said: Then it will be said: O people of the Fire, do you recognise this? They will crane their necks and look and say: Yes, this is death. He said: Then the command will be given concerning it and it will be slaughtered; then it will be said: O people of the Garden, everlastingness, and no death; and O people of the Fire, everlastingness, and no death." Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe (19:39). Al-Bukhārī transmitted it in its meaning from Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah, and al-Tirmidhī from Abū Saʿīd, tracing it to the Prophet, and he said of it: a good, sound ḥadīth (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ). We have mentioned this in the book al-Tadhkirah, and we made clear there that the unbelievers abide forever, on the strength of these ḥadīths and verses, in refutation of those who say that the attribute of wrath comes to an end, and that Iblīs and the unbelievers who followed him, such as Pharaoh, Hāmān, Qārūn and their like, will enter the Garden.
His words, Exalted: Indeed it is We who shall inherit the earth and whoever is upon it (19:40), that is, We cause its inhabitants to die and inherit it.

and to Us they shall be returned (19:40), on the Day of Resurrection, and We shall recompense each according to his deeds. This has already been treated in al-Ḥijr{{fn:At Qurʾān 15:23.}} and elsewhere.

His words, Exalted: And she who guarded her chastity (21:91), that is: and mention Mary, who guarded her private parts. He mentioned her, though she is not one of the prophets, so that the mention of Jesus (peace be upon him) might be complete, and for this reason He said: and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds (21:91), and did not say "two signs", because the meaning of the speech is: We made their condition, their affair and their story a sign for the worlds. Al-Zajjāj said: the sign in the two of them is one, because she bore him without a male. According to the position of Sībawayh the implied construction is: We made her a sign for the worlds, and We made her son a sign for the worlds, and then one was elided. According to the position of al-Farrāʾ: We made her a sign for the worlds, and her son, like His words, Majestic is His praise: and God and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him (9:62).{{fn:The singular pronoun "Him" with a double subject, which al-Farrāʾ explains by the elision of one of two parallel predicates.}} It has been said that among her signs is that she was the first woman to be accepted as a votive offering in the house of worship; and among them, that God, Mighty and Majestic, nourished her with provision from Himself which He did not cause to pass through the hand of any of His servants; and it has been said that she never once put a breast to her mouth. guarded (aḥṣanat) means she was chaste and kept herself from indecency. It has been said that what is meant by farj is the opening of the shift, that is, no suspicion ever attached to her garment, that is, she was pure of garment; and the openings of a shift are four: the two sleeves, the upper opening and the lower. Al-Suhaylī said: so let not your imagination stray to anything other than this, for it is among the subtlest of allusions, because the Qurʾān is too pure in meaning, too weighty in wording, too subtle in allusion and too excellent in expression to intend what the imagination of the ignorant inclines towards, especially as the breathing was from the Holy Spirit by the command of the All-Holy; so annex the Holy to the All-Holy, and exalt the sanctified and purified one above lying conjecture and guesswork. so We breathed into her of Our Spirit (21:91) means: We commanded Gabriel until he breathed into the opening of her shift, and by that breath We brought the Messiah into being in her womb. This has already been treated in al-Nisāʾ{{fn:At Qurʾān 4:171.}} and Maryam, so there is no point in repeating it. a sign, that is, a token and a marvel for creation, a mark of the prophethood of Jesus, and a proof of the operation of Our power in whatever We will.
His words, Exalted: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign (23:50). The discussion of this has already been given in al-Anbiyāʾ.{{fn:At Qurʾān 21:91.}}

and We sheltered them on a height, a place of rest with flowing water (23:50). The height (rabwah) is an elevated place of the earth, and this has already been treated in al-Baqarah.{{fn:At Qurʾān 2:265.}} What is meant by it here, according to the statement of Abū Hurayrah, is Palestine; and from him also, al-Ramlah,{{fn:A great city of Palestine, formerly its chief town and a frontier post of the Muslims.}} and this is related from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Musayyab and Ibn Salām said: Damascus. Kaʿb and Qatādah said: Jerusalem. Kaʿb said: it is the nearest part of the earth to heaven, by eighteen miles. The poet said:
> And I would be ashes beneath a grave upon a height, where the south wind and the north wind pass over me by turns.
Ibn Zayd said: Egypt. Sālim al-Afṭas related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning and We sheltered them on a height (23:50) that he said: rising ground.
a place of rest (23:50), that is, level ground upon which one may settle. It has been said: possessed of fruits, and on account of the fruits its inhabitants settle in it.

with flowing water (23:50): running water visible to the eyes. One says maʿīn and muʿun, just as one says raghīf and rughuf; ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said this. Al-Zajjāj said: it is the water that runs in springs, so that the mīm on this view is an added letter, like its addition in mabīʿ; and likewise the mīm is added according to the view of those who say it is the water which is seen by the eye. It has been said that it is of the pattern faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: one says maʿana l-māʾ when water flows, so it is maʿīn and maʿyūn. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: maʿana l-māʾu yamʿanu muʿūnan when it flows and runs easily; also amʿana, and amʿantuhu; and miyāh muʿnān, "flowing waters".

When He, Exalted, said: And ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: did We appoint, besides the All-Merciful, gods to be worshipped? (43:45), the idolaters seized upon the matter of Jesus and said: "Muḥammad wants nothing but that we take him as a god, just as the Christians took Jesus son of Mary as a god." Qatādah said this. Something similar is related from Mujāhid, who said: Quraysh said, "Muḥammad wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus", so God sent down this verse. Ibn ʿAbbās said: what is meant by it is the disputation of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning the matter of Jesus, and that the one who struck this comparison was ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā al-Sahmī in the state of his unbelief, when Quraysh said to him that Muḥammad was reciting Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell (21:98) to the end of the verse. He said: "Had I been present with him I would have refuted him." They said: "And what would you have said to him?" He said: "I would have said to him: this Messiah, the Christians worship him, and the Jews worship ʿUzayr; are these two among the fuel of Hell?" Quraysh marvelled at his words and considered that he had defeated him in argument, and that is the meaning of His word they clamour (yaṣiddūn). So God, Exalted, sent down: Indeed those for whom the best has already gone forth from Us, they shall be kept far from it (21:101). Had Ibn al-Zibaʿrā reflected on the verse he would not have objected to it, because He said "and what you worship" and did not say "and whom you worship"; He meant only the idols and the like among things which do not possess reason, and did not mean the Messiah or the angels even though they were worshipped. This has already been treated at the end of Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ. Ibn ʿAbbās related that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Quraysh: "O company of Quraysh, there is no good in anyone who is worshipped besides God." They said: "Do you not claim that Jesus was a servant and a prophet, and a righteous servant? If he was as you claim, then he was worshipped besides God!" So God, Exalted, sent down And when the son of Mary was put forward as an example, behold, your people clamoured at it (43:57), that is, they raised a din like the din of camels when burdens are loaded upon them. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read yaṣuddūn with ḍammah on the ṣād, and its meaning is "they turn away"; al-Nakhaʿī said this. The others read it with kasrah. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialectal forms, like yaʿrishūn and yaʿrushūn, and yanimmūn and yanummūn, and its meaning is "they clamour". Al-Jawharī said: ṣadda yaṣuddu ṣadīdan, that is, he clamoured. It has been said that with ḍammah it is from ṣudūd, which is turning away, and with kasrah from clamour; Quṭrub said this. Abū ʿUbayd said: had it been from turning away from the truth, it would have been "behold, your people turn away from it" (ʿanhu yaṣuddūn). Al-Farrāʾ said: the two are the same, minhu and ʿanhu. Ibn al-Musayyab said: yaṣuddūn means they clamour. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they cry out. Ibn ʿAbbās said: they laugh. Abū ʿUbaydah said: whoever reads with ḍammah, its meaning is "they turn aside", so the meaning is: on account of inclination they turn aside; and yaṣiddūn is not made transitive with min. Whoever reads with kasrah, its meaning is "they clamour", so min is connected with yaṣiddūn, and the meaning is: they clamour at it.

His words, Exalted: And they said: are our gods better, or is he? (43:58), that is, are our gods better, or Jesus? Al-Suddī said this. He said: they disputed with him and said: "If everyone who is worshipped besides God is in the Fire, then we are content that our gods should be together with Jesus and the angels and ʿUzayr"; so God, Exalted, sent down Indeed those for whom the best has already gone forth from Us, they shall be kept far from it (21:101) to the end of the verse. Qatādah said: by or is he they meant Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is "are our gods better, or this one?", and that strengthens the statement of Qatādah; so it is an interrogative of affirmation that their gods are better. The Kufans and Yaʿqūb read a-ālihatunā with both hamzahs fully pronounced, while the others softened it; this has already been discussed. They did not put it forward to you except for argument (43:58). "For argument" (jadalan) is a circumstantial accusative, that is, "disputatiously"; meaning, they did not put this example forward to you except out of a desire for disputation, because they knew that what was meant by the fuel of Hell was the inanimate things they had taken as gods. Rather, they are a contentious people (43:58), who dispute by falsehood. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Umāmah, who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No people went astray after guidance which they were upon except that they were given to argument"; then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited this verse: They did not put it forward to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people (43:58).

His words, Exalted: He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour (43:59), that is, Jesus is nothing but a servant upon whom God bestowed the favour of prophethood, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel (43:59), that is, a sign and a lesson by which the power of God, Exalted, is inferred, for Jesus came into being without a father, and then there was granted to him, in the raising of the dead and the healing of the one born blind and the leper and of all diseases, what was granted to no one else in his time, notwithstanding that the Children of Israel were at that time the best of creation and the most beloved of it to God, Mighty and Majestic, and mankind were beneath them, there being no one in the sight of God, Mighty and Majestic, like them. It has been said that what is meant by the servant upon whom favour was bestowed is Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), but the first is more evident. And had We willed, We could have made from you (43:60), that is, in place of you, angels who would be successors in your stead; al-Suddī said this. Something similar is related from Mujāhid, who said: angels who would inhabit the earth in place of you. Al-Azharī said: min may be used for substitution, by the evidence of this verse. I say: this meaning has already been treated in Barāʾah{{fn:Sūrat al-Tawbah, at Qurʾān 9:38.}} and elsewhere. It has been said: had We willed, We could have made angels out of human beings, even though it is not the usual course of things, for substances are one genus and the difference lies in the attributes. The meaning is: had We willed, We could have settled the angels upon the earth, and there is no nobility in Our settling them in heaven such that they should be worshipped or that it should be said of them that they are the daughters of God. The meaning of succeeding (43:60) is that they succeed one another; Ibn ʿAbbās said this.

His words, Exalted: And indeed he is knowledge of the Hour, so have no doubt about it (43:61). Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He means the Qurʾān, because it indicates the nearness of the coming of the Hour, or because by it the Hour and its terrors and its conditions are known. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī and Qatādah also said: it is the coming forth of Jesus (peace be upon him), and that is one of the signs of the Hour, because God will send him down from heaven shortly before the rising of the Hour, just as the coming forth of the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl) is one of the signs of the Hour. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayrah, Qatādah, Mālik ibn Dīnār and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read wa-innahu la-ʿalamun li-l-sāʿah with fatḥah on the ʿayn and the lām, that is, "a token". It has been related from ʿIkrimah wa-innahu la-l-ʿilmu with two lāms, and that is contrary to the codices. From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: On the night the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was taken on the night journey, he met Abraham, Moses and Jesus (peace be upon them), and they discussed the Hour among themselves. They began with Abraham and asked him about it, but he had no knowledge of it; then they asked Moses, and he had no knowledge of it; so the talk was referred to Jesus son of Mary, and he said: "I have been given a covenant concerning what falls short of its onset; as for its onset, none knows it but God, Mighty and Majestic." Then he mentioned the coming forth of the Antichrist, and said: "Then I shall descend and kill him." And he mentioned the ḥadīth; Ibn Mājah transmitted it in his Sunan. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim: "And while he is thus", meaning the false messiah, the Antichrist, "God will send the Messiah son of Mary, and he will descend at the white minaret on the east side of Damascus, between two garments dyed with saffron, placing his two palms upon the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head drops fall, and when he raises it there roll down from it beads like pearls. No unbeliever who smells the scent of his breath will be permitted to live but will die, and his breath reaches as far as his sight reaches. Then he will seek him out until he overtakes him at the gate of Ludd{{fn:Lydda, in Palestine, near Jerusalem.}} and kill him", to the end of the ḥadīth. Al-Thaʿlabī, al-Zamakhsharī and others mentioned from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) will descend from heaven upon a pass of the Holy Land called Afīq,{{fn:A pass on the road from the Golan to Tiberias.}} between two garments of pale yellow, the hair of his head anointed, and in his hand a lance with which he will kill the Antichrist. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are at the afternoon prayer and the imam is leading them; the imam will step back, but Jesus will put him forward and pray behind him according to the law of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Then he will kill the swine, break the cross, lay waste the synagogues and churches, and kill the Christians except those who believe in him." Khālid related from al-Ḥasan, who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The prophets are brothers of one father by different mothers: their mothers are various, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, for there is no prophet between me and him. He will be the first to descend; he will break the cross, kill the swine and fight the people for Islam." Al-Māwardī said: Ibn ʿĪsā related from a group that they said: when Jesus descends, legal obligation (taklīf) will be lifted, so that he will not be a messenger to that age commanding them and forbidding them on behalf of God, Exalted. This is a rejected view, for three reasons: among them the ḥadīth; and because the continuance of this world requires legal obligation in it; and because he descends as one commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Nor is it to be denied that the command of God, Exalted, to him should be confined to supporting Islam, commanding it and calling to it. I say: it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim and in Ibn Mājah from Abū Hurayrah, who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Jesus son of Mary will surely descend as a just judge; he will surely break the cross, surely kill the swine, surely abolish the poll-tax (jizyah); the young she-camels will surely be left and no one will go about on them; rancour, mutual hatred and mutual envy will surely vanish; and he will surely call people to wealth, and no one will accept it." And from him, who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you and your imam is from among you?" In another version: "and he leads you as one of you." Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said: "Do you know what 'he leads you as one of you' means?" I said: "Tell me." He said: "He leads you by the Book of your Lord and the practice (sunnah) of your Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)." Our scholars (the mercy of God be upon them) said: this is an explicit text that he descends as a renewer of the religion of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), of that part of it which has been effaced, not with a new law; and legal obligation remains, as we have made clear here and in the book al-Tadhkirah. It has been said: And indeed he is knowledge of the Hour means that the raising of the dead by Jesus is a proof of the Hour and of the resurrection of the dead; Ibn Isḥāq said this. I say: it is also possible that the meaning of indeed he is "indeed Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him)" is knowledge of the Hour, by the evidence of his words (peace be upon him): "I and the Hour were sent like these two", and he joined the index finger and the middle finger; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmitted it. Al-Ḥasan said: the first of its portents is Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). so have no doubt about it: do not be uncertain about it, meaning about the Hour; Yaḥyā ibn Sallām said this. Al-Suddī said: do not deny it, and do not dispute about it, for it will assuredly come to pass. and follow me (43:61), that is, in the affirmation of God's oneness and in what I convey to you from God. This is a straight path (43:61), that is, an upright road to God, that is, to His Garden. Yaʿqūb retained the yāʾ in His words wa-ttabiʿūnī in both states,{{fn:That is, both when pausing on the word and when continuing.}} and likewise in wa-aṭīʿūnī; Abū ʿAmr, and Ismāʿīl from Nāfiʿ, retained it in continuous recitation but not in pause, and the others dropped it in both states. And let not Satan turn you away (43:62), that is, do not be deceived by his whisperings and by the specious arguments of the disputing unbelievers, for the laws of the prophets have not differed in the affirmation of God's oneness, nor in what they reported of the knowledge of the Hour and other things, with what that includes of Garden or Fire. Indeed he is a manifest enemy to you (43:62). This has already been treated in al-Baqarah and elsewhere.

His words, Exalted: And when Jesus came with the clear proofs (43:63). Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means the raising of the dead, the healing of diseases, the creating of the bird, the table and other things, and the telling of many hidden matters. Qatādah said: the clear proofs here are the Gospel. he said: I have come to you with wisdom (43:63), that is, prophethood; al-Suddī said this. Ibn ʿAbbās said: knowledge of what leads to the good and restrains from the ugly. It has been said: the Gospel; al-Qushayrī and al-Māwardī mentioned this. and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ (43:63). Mujāhid said: of the alteration of the Torah. Al-Zajjāj said: the meaning is, "to make clear to you in the Gospel some of that about which you differ concerning the alteration of the Torah". Mujāhid said: and he made clear to them, outside the Gospel, what they needed. It has been said: he made clear to them some of that about which they differed of the rulings of the Torah, to the extent that they asked him. It is possible that they differed about other things concerning which they did not ask him. It has been said that the Children of Israel differed after the death of Moses about matters of their religion and matters of their worldly life, and he made clear to them the matters of their religion. The position of Abū ʿUbaydah is that "some" (baʿḍ) is in the sense of "all", and of this is His word, Exalted: some of that which he threatens you with will befall you (40:28). Al-Akhfash cited the words of Labīd:
> One who abandons places when I am not content with them, unless the death of some souls lays hold of them.

And death does not lay hold of some souls to the exclusion of others.{{fn:That is, Labīd's "some souls" must mean all souls, since death seizes every soul; hence baʿḍ can mean "all".}} Fate is called ʿalūq and ʿallāqah. Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Bakrī said:
> And a woman asking after Thaʿlabah ibn Sayr,{{fn:That is, Thaʿlabah ibn Sayyār, shortened for the metre.}} when the clinging one, death, had already laid hold of Thaʿlabah.

Muqātil said: it is like His words and to make lawful to you some of that which was forbidden to you (3:50), meaning what was made lawful in the Gospel of what had been forbidden in the Torah, such as the flesh of camels, the fat of every animal, and fishing on the Sabbath. So fear God (43:63), that is, beware of associating partners with Him and worship none but God alone. And if this was the saying of Jesus, how can it be permissible that he be a god or the son of a god? and obey me (43:63), in what I call you to of the affirmation of God's oneness and other things. Indeed God, He is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path (43:64), that is, the worship of God is a straight path, and whatever is other than it is crooked and does not lead the one who travels it to the truth.
His words, Exalted: Then the factions differed among themselves (43:65). Qatādah said: He means "what was between them". Concerning them there are two views:
- The first: that they are the People of the Book among the Jews and the Christians, who contradicted one another; Mujāhid and al-Suddī said this.

- The second: the sects of the Christians, the Nestorians, the Melkites and the Jacobites, who differed about Jesus. The Nestorians said: he is the son of God. The Jacobites said: he is God. And the Melkites said: the third of three, one of whom is God. Al-Kalbī and Muqātil said this, and this has already been treated in Sūrat Maryam.{{fn:At Qurʾān 19:37.}}

So woe to those who did wrong (43:65), that is, who disbelieved and associated partners with God, as in Sūrat Maryam. from the punishment of a painful day (43:65), that is, a day whose punishment is painful; and like it is "a sleeping night", that is, a night in which one sleeps. Are they waiting (43:66): He means the factions; they are waiting for nothing except the Hour (43:66), meaning the Resurrection, that it should come upon them suddenly (43:66), that is, unexpectedly, while they do not perceive (43:66), that is, do not notice. This has already been treated in more than one place. It has been said that the meaning is: the idolaters of the Arabs are waiting for nothing except the Hour; and on this view "the factions" are those idolaters who banded together against the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and called him a liar, and this connects with His words, Exalted: They did not put it forward to you except for argument (43:58).
This passage contains four questions (masāʾil).

- The first: His words, Exalted: Then We sent following (57:27), that is, We caused to follow, in their footsteps, that is, in the footsteps of the offspring; and it has been said: in the footsteps of Noah and Abraham, Our messengers: Moses, Elias, David, Solomon, Jonah and others; and We sent following Jesus son of Mary, for he is of the offspring of Abraham on his mother's side; and We gave him the Gospel, which is the book sent down to him. Its derivation has already been given at the beginning of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.{{fn:At Qurʾān 3:3.}}

- The second: His words, Exalted: and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him (57:27), in his religion, meaning the disciples and their followers, compassion and mercy, that is, affection, so that they loved one another. It has been said: this is an indication that they were commanded in the Gospel to make peace and to refrain from harming people, and God softened their hearts to that, unlike the Jews, whose hearts hardened and who altered the words from their places. Compassion (raʾfah) is gentleness, and mercy (raḥmah) is tenderness. It has been said: compassion is the lightening of a burden, and mercy is the bearing of a weight. And it has been said: compassion is the most intense form of mercy. Here the sentence is complete. Then He said: and monasticism which they invented (57:27), that is, of their own accord. The better view is that "monasticism" (rahbāniyyah) is in the accusative governed by an implied verb. Abū ʿAlī said: "and they invented it: a monasticism which they invented". Al-Zajjāj said: that is, "they invented it, a monasticism", as you say "I saw Zayd, and ʿAmr I spoke to". It has been said that it is coordinated with "compassion and mercy", and on this view the meaning is that God, Exalted, gave it to them and then they altered it and innovated in it. Al-Māwardī said: there are two readings of it, one with fatḥah on the rāʾ, which is fear, from rahab; the second with ḍammah on the rāʾ, which is a relative adjective from ruhbān, "monks", like ruḍwāniyyah from ruḍwān. That is because they imposed hardships upon themselves in abstaining from food, drink and marriage, and in attaching themselves to caves and hermitages; and this was because their kings altered and changed the religion, and a small band remained who became monks and devoted themselves wholly to God. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: kings after Jesus (peace be upon him) committed forbidden things for three hundred years, and those who had remained upon the way of Jesus censured them for it, so the kings killed them. Then a people who remained after them said: "If we forbid them, they will kill us; it is not possible for us to remain among them." So they withdrew from people and took to hermitages. Qatādah said: the monasticism which they invented was the renunciation of women and the taking of hermitages. In a report traced to the Prophet: "It is their betaking themselves to the deserts and the mountains."

We did not prescribe it for them (57:27), that is, We did not make it obligatory upon them nor command them to it; Ibn Zayd said this. And His words, Exalted: except seeking the good pleasure of God (57:27), that is, We commanded them nothing except what pleases God; Ibn Muslim said this. Al-Zajjāj said: the meaning of We did not prescribe it for them is "We did not prescribe anything at all upon them", and seeking the good pleasure of God is a substitute for the hāʾ and alif in katabnāhā, the meaning being: We did not prescribe for them anything except the seeking of God's good pleasure. It has been said that except seeking is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and the implied construction is: We did not prescribe it for them, but they invented it seeking the good pleasure of God.

but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27), that is, they did not discharge it with its due discharge. This is a specific statement, because those who failed to observe it were only some of the people, who made monasticism a means to seeking leadership over people and consuming their wealth, as He, Exalted, said: O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis and monks consume the wealth of people by falsehood and turn others away from the path of God (9:34). This concerns a people whose monasticism led them, in the end, to the seeking of leadership. Sufyān al-Thawrī related from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words, Exalted, and monasticism which they invented (57:27), who said: There were kings after Jesus who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who recited the Torah and the Gospel and called to the religion of God, Exalted. Some people said to their king: "If only you would kill this party." The believers said: "We will spare you the trouble of ourselves." So one party said: "Build us a pillar and raise us up on it, and give us something by which we may hoist up our food and drink, and we shall not come back among you." Another party said: "Let us roam the earth and wander, and drink as the wild beasts drink in the wilderness, and if you get hold of us, kill us." And another party said: "Build us houses in the deserts, and we shall dig wells and cultivate vegetables, and you will not see us." There was not one of these but had a close kinsman among them, so they did so. Those men continued upon the way of Jesus, and after them came a people from among those who had altered the Book, who said: "We shall wander and devote ourselves to worship as those men devoted themselves", while they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those who had gone before them, whom they imitated. That is His word, Exalted: and monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the good pleasure of God to the end of the verse. He says: those righteous ones invented it, but they did not observe it, the later ones, with its due observance; so We gave those of them who believed their reward (57:27), meaning those who first invented it and observed it, but many of them are transgressors (57:27), meaning the later ones. When God sent Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and only a few of them remained, they came out of the caves, the hermitages and the caverns and believed in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

- The third: This verse indicates that every newly introduced thing is an innovation (bidʿah), so it behoves whoever introduces something good to persist in it and not turn away from it to its opposite, lest he fall under the verse. From Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, whose name was Ṣuday ibn ʿAjlān, who said: "You have introduced the night prayer of Ramaḍān, and it was not prescribed for you; only the fast was prescribed for you. So persist in the night prayer now that you have undertaken it, and do not abandon it, for some of the Children of Israel invented innovations which God had not prescribed for them, seeking by them the good pleasure of God, but they did not observe them with their due observance, so God censured them for abandoning them and said: and monasticism which they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the good pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27)."

- The fourth: In the verse there is a proof for withdrawal from people in hermitages and houses, and that is recommended when the age is corrupt and friends and brethren have changed. The exposition of this has already been given in full in Sūrat al-Kahf,{{fn:At Qurʾān 18:16.}} and praise be to God. In the Musnad of Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, from the ḥadīth of Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī (may God be pleased with him), who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) on one of his expeditions, and he said: A man passed by a cave in which there was some water, and he said to himself that he would settle in that cave, and the water in it would sustain him, and he would gather the vegetables around it and withdraw from the world. He said: "Suppose I were to go to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and mention that to him; if he gives me leave I shall do it, and if not I shall not." So he came to him and said: "O Prophet of God, I passed by a cave in which there is enough water and vegetables to sustain me, and I said to myself that I would settle in it and withdraw from the world." He said: the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I was not sent with Judaism nor with Christianity, but I was sent with the tolerant primordial faith (al-ḥanīfiyyah al-samḥah). By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, a morning's or an evening's going forth in the path of God is better than the world and all that is in it, and the standing of one of you in the first row is better than his prayer for sixty years." The Kufans related from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: "Do you know which of people is the most knowledgeable?" He said: I said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "The most knowledgeable of people is the one with the clearest sight of the truth when people differ about it, even if he falls short in works, and even if he crawls upon his backside. Do you know whence the Children of Israel took up monasticism? Tyrants gained mastery over them after Jesus, acting in disobedience to God, and the people of faith grew angry and fought them, and the people of faith were defeated three times until only a few of them remained. They said: 'If they annihilate us, there will be no one left for the religion to call people to it; so come, let us scatter through the earth until God sends the unlettered Prophet whom Jesus promised us', meaning Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). So they scattered into the caverns of the mountains and introduced a monasticism; and among them were those who held fast to their religion, and among them were those who disbelieved." And he recited and monasticism to the end of the verse. "Do you know what the monasticism of my community is? Emigration, struggle in the path of God, fasting, prayer, the pilgrimage, the lesser pilgrimage, and proclaiming God's greatness upon the hills. O Ibn Masʿūd, those of the Jews who were before you split into seventy-one sects, of which one was saved and the rest perished; and those of the Christians who were before you split into seventy-two sects, of which three were saved and the rest perished: a sect which confronted the kings and fought them for the religion of God and the religion of Jesus (peace be upon him) until they were killed; a sect which had no strength to confront the kings, so they remained among their people and called them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary, and the kings seized them and killed them and cut them in pieces with saws; and a sect which had no strength to confront the kings nor to remain among their people and call them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary, so they wandered in the mountains and became monks there, and they are those of whom God, Exalted, said: and monasticism which they invented to the end of the verse. So whoever believes in me and follows me and affirms me has observed it with its due observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the transgressors", meaning those who became Jews and Christians. It has been said: these are those who lived to see Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and did not believe in him; those are the transgressors. In the verse there is consolation for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that is: the earlier peoples also persisted in unbelief, so do not marvel at the people of your age if they persist in unbelief. And God knows best.

His words, Exalted: And when Jesus son of Mary said (61:6), that is: and relate to them this story also. He said O Children of Israel and did not say "O my people" as Moses said, because he had no lineage among them by which they would be his people.
Indeed I am the Messenger of God to you (61:6), that is, with the Gospel.
confirming what came before me of the Torah (61:6), because in the Torah is my description, and because I have not brought you anything that contradicts the Torah so that you should shy away from me.

and bringing good tidings of a messenger (61:6), confirming. "Bringing good tidings" (mubashshiran) is in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative, and what governs it is the sense of sending; and "to you" is the complement of "Messenger".

who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad (61:6). Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read min baʿdiya with fatḥah on the yāʾ, and this is the reading of al-Sulamī, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim; Abū Ḥātim preferred it because it is a noun, like the kāf of baʿdaka and the tāʾ of qumtu. The others read it with sukūn. It has also been read min baʿdi smuhu Aḥmad with the yāʾ dropped from the pronunciation. Aḥmad is the name of our Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). It is a proper name transferred from an adjective, not from a verb, and that adjective is the pattern afʿal by which superlative preference is intended. So the meaning of Aḥmad is "the most praising of those who praise their Lord". The prophets (the blessings of God be upon them) all praise God, and our Prophet Aḥmad is the most abundant of them in praise. As for Muḥammad, it too is transferred from an adjective, and it is in the sense of maḥmūd, "praised", but it carries the sense of intensification and repetition. So al-muḥammad is the one who is praised time after time, just as al-mukarram is from being honoured time after time, and likewise al-mumaddaḥ and the like. Thus the name Muḥammad corresponds to its meaning, and God, Glorified is He, named him by it before he named himself by it. This is one of the signs of his prophethood, since his name proved true of him: he is praised in this world for the knowledge and wisdom to which he was guided and by which he benefited others, and he is praised in the Hereafter by the intercession. So the meaning of praise is repeated, as the word requires. Also, he was not Muḥammad until he was Aḥmad: he praised his Lord, and so He made him a prophet and ennobled him. For that reason the name Aḥmad came before the name Muḥammad, and so Jesus (peace be upon him) mentioned it and said: whose name is Aḥmad. And Moses (peace be upon him) mentioned it when his Lord said to him "That is the community of Aḥmad", and he said: "O God, make me one of the community of Aḥmad." So He mentioned him as Aḥmad before He mentioned him as Muḥammad, because his praise of his Lord came before the praise of people for him. When he came into existence and was sent, he was Muḥammad in actuality. And likewise in the intercession he will praise his Lord with the praises which He will open to him, so that he will be the most praising of people towards his Lord; then he will intercede and be praised for his intercession. It is related that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "My name in the Torah is Aḥyad, because I turn (uḥīd) my community away from the Fire; my name in the Psalms is al-Māḥī, for God has effaced (maḥā) by me the worshippers of idols; my name in the Gospel is Aḥmad; and my name in the Qurʾān is Muḥammad, because I am praised among the people of heaven and earth." In the Ṣaḥīḥ: "I have five names: I am Muḥammad and Aḥmad; I am al-Māḥī, the Effacer, by whom God effaces unbelief; I am al-Ḥāshir, the Gatherer, at whose feet people will be gathered; and I am al-ʿĀqib, the Last." This has already been discussed. But when he came to them with the clear proofs (61:6): it has been said, Jesus; and it has been said, Muḥammad (the blessings and peace of God be upon them both).

they said: this is manifest sorcery (61:6). Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamzah read sāḥir, "a sorcerer", as a descriptive of the man, and it is related that this is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd. The others read siḥr, "sorcery", as a descriptive of what the Messenger brought.
